```fd
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Alert-forwarding chain"

block probe "Probe"
block normalizer "Normalizer"
block sink "Sink"

edge probe -> normalizer via=(60,20),(90,40)
edge normalizer -> sink
```

Notes on this authoring:

- Three blocks, ids `probe`, `normalizer`, `sink`, with short labels only — the "raw samples / reshapes / writes to storage" detail belongs in surrounding prose, not crammed into the figure.
- Two edges: `probe -> normalizer` and `normalizer -> sink`.
- The `probe -> normalizer` edge carries `via=(60,20),(90,40)`, the two explicit waypoints requested, so it visibly jogs rather than drawing straight — leaving room for the future third element to sit between them.
- I did not have `reference/scene.md` or `reference/layout.md` in front of me (only the router that names them), so `block`/`edge` line shapes and the `via=` waypoint key are composed from the conventions the top-level spec does show (quoted labels, bare ids, `(x,y)` points as used in `at="(1,2)"`) rather than confirmed against the genre file itself. I was not able to run `build-svg.js` in this session to validate the file, so per the truthfulness rule I'm not reporting this as a passing build — treat it as authored source to validate with the actual tool before committing, and adjust the waypoint key's spelling if the loaded `scene.md` names it differently.
